# moa-brainstorm: next cross-token comparison after verified mathematical nulls

Mode: independent scientific brainstorm.

Reconstruct the situation from the supplied evidence. Propose distinct mechanisms, including an
implementation error, an objective or gradient mismatch, and an unintended learning dynamic when
relevant. For each, give a falsifiable prediction and the cheapest discriminating check. State
what is observed versus inferred. Do not choose a winner.

## Context (what was run and what it showed)

Model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B rev 851bf6e8. A suppression detector scores vocabulary tokens that RISE
from EARLY layer 23 to PEAK layer 25 and FALL by OUTPUT layer 32. Per token position it builds
an orthonormal basis from the top-ranked suppressed token directions; the "suppressed component"
of a residual is its projection onto that basis, c_p = component(residual_p, B_p).

First screen (GPU, L23, rank-1, C=2.0, last-3 prompt positions, 32-token continuations):
mean pairwise signed cosine of c_p across the 3 positions was 0.002-0.05 for spider (source),
dog and ant (donors), and a same-form neutral control. A rank-1 edit along the mean component
direction ("signed consensus"), the avg-projector span direction, and a matched-random control
ALL left p(8) at 0.86-0.88 (base 0.8826) and the continuation "8. Hypothesis: The animal that
spins webs has 8 legs." with spider identity intact in every condition, including controls.

## Mathematical nulls found in review (verified numerically, these are facts)

The first draft over-read three statistics. These nulls are now established:

1. At T=3 positions, the mean pairwise cosine of mean-centered vectors is mechanically -1/2
   whenever norms are comparable (centering forces sum z_i = 0, so the mean over six ordered
   pairs is -sum ||z_i||^2 / 6). Observed -0.49 = the null exactly. The centered statistic
   carries only norm-spread information at T=3. Any "anti-alignment" reading is void.
2. The consensus ratio ||mean(c_p)|| / mean(||c_p||) has null 1/sqrt(3) = 0.577 for three
   equal-norm orthogonal vectors. Observed 0.62-0.65.
3. The avg-projector top eigenvalue has null 1/3 = 0.333 for orthogonal per-position rank-1
   bases. Observed 0.437-0.499.

## Two design limits of the first screen (facts)

4. Components were measured at EARLY layer 23, but the detector selects tokens that rise by
   PEAK 25 and fall by 32. Low alignment before the rise cannot reject post-rise agreement.
5. Only last-3-position mean statistics were recorded; a mean can hide a single useful token
   pair. The user's proposal is about agreement from 2+ tokens.

## The planned next family (constrained; no new framework, no hyperparameter grid)

Build ONE bank of clean trajectories (source, dog, ant, control): full residuals, per-position
token labels, detector scores (top-64 + named tokens: spider/dog/ant/webs/animal/legs), and the
per-position detector bases, saved to disk so all analysis is GPU-free and repeatable. Then
GPU-free: full pairwise signed cosines AND norms of c_p at EARLY 23, PEAK 25 and OUTPUT 32,
over all prompt positions (not just last-3), with token labels attached; direct
source-vs-control alignment; orthogonal and matched-random nulls for every scalar; a
peak-vs-early comparison. Check detector scores for near-zero/tied selections.

## Questions

1. Given the nulls, what scalar or vector statistic genuinely distinguishes "a reusable signed
   concept direction appears at the suppression peak" from "orthogonal-ish nuisance plus a
   shared mean"? Define it, its null distribution, and what observation would refute the
   user's proposal versus support it.
2. At which measurement layer should agreement be computed for the detector's selection to be
   meaningful, and what exactly would a peak-vs-early increase in agreement show (and not
   show)? Note the detector itself is defined by the rise-then-fall; is measuring AT the peak
   circular in any way that needs a control?
3. Position set matters: the prompt is "Fact: The number of legs on the animal that spins webs
   is ". Which positions (animal mention, property phrase, final "is ") could carry a
   concept-level signal that the last-3 window misses, and what would distinguish a real
   concept-position signal from syntax-position confound?
4. What is the cheapest causal follow-up if (and only if) a peak-layer agreement survives the
   nulls and is concept-specific beyond same-format controls? Constraint: fixed common
   replacement procedure, selector change only, correct perturbation controls, both animals,
   full continuations.
5. If NO statistic survives the nulls at any layer, what is the honest next mechanism to test
   instead (suppression-state varies by layer/token, per the user's other hypothesis), and what
   measurement distinguishes it from "the detector is noise" without a big sweep?

State uncertainties. Do not optimize for agreement.
